en: Udāna 3.7 Sakkudānasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Now on that occasion the Venerable Mahākassapa was dwelling in the Pippali Cave; having attained a certain meditative concentration, he remained seated cross-legged for seven days.
Then, with the passing of those seven days, the Venerable Mahākassapa emerged from that concentration.
Then, as the Venerable Mahākassapa arose from that concentration, it occurred to him:
"What if I were now to enter Rājagaha for alms?
At that time, about five hundred deities were making an effort to provide almsfood for the Venerable Mahākassapa.
Then the Venerable Mahākassapa, having declined those five hundred deities, dressed in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Rājagaha for alms.
Now at that time, Sakka, lord of the devas, desired to give almsfood to the Venerable Mahākassapa;
having manifested himself in the form of a weaver, he was weaving thread, while the asura maiden Sujā filled the shuttle.
Then the Venerable Mahākassapa, wandering for alms from house to house in Rājagaha, approached the residence of Sakka, the lord of the devas.
Sakka, the lord of the devas, saw the Venerable Mahākassapa coming from afar.

Upon seeing him, he went out from his house, went forward to meet him, took the bowl from his hand, entered the house, scooped rice from a jar, filled the bowl, and gave it to the Venerable Mahākassapa.
Thus the alms-food became possessed of many soups, many sauces, and many flavorful sauces.
Then it occurred to the Venerable Mahākassapa:
"What being is this, who possesses such power and majesty?"
Then it occurred to the Venerable Mahākassapa:
"This is Sakka, the lord of the devas.
Having understood this, he said this to Sakka, the lord of the devas:
“Kosiya, you have done this; do not do such a thing again.
“Venerable Kassapa, we too have need of merit.”
“We too must perform meritorious deeds.

Then Sakka, lord of the devas, paid homage to the Venerable Mahākassapa, circumambulated him keeping him to his right, and ascending into the air, he uttered this inspired exclamation three times in the sky:
“Oh, what a gift! What a supreme gift! It is well-established upon Kassapa!”
“Oh, what a gift! What a supreme gift, well-established upon Kassapa!
Oh, what a gift! What a supreme gift, well-established upon Kassapa!

Then the Blessed One, with the divine ear-element, purified and surpassing that of humans, heard Sakka, lord of the devas, as he rose into the air and, in the sky, uttered this inspired exclamation three times:
“Oh, what a gift! What a supreme gift, well-established in Kassapa!
Oh, what a gift! What a supreme gift, well-established in Kassapa!
Oh, what a gift! What a supreme gift, well-established in Kassapa!”
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“For the bhikkhu who lives on alms,
who sustains himself and does not support others;”
The gods envy such a one,
who is tranquil, ever mindful.
Thus ends the seventh [verse].
